To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
facilitation of passive avoidancelearning can be induced in day-old chicks by a brief stressor, and that the effect is mediated by the glucocorticoid system.
facilitation of memory recall in the day-old chicks can be achieved by behavioral stress, and that the effect is mediated by the glucocorticoid system.

behavioral "stressing," such as social isolation, can facilitate recall of a weak passive avoidance task in day-old chicks and that the mechanism of this facilitation appears to involve the glucocorticoid receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of isolation on learning and memory.
the effects of stress on learning and memory in the young chick.
the role of stress hormones in memory consolidation in day-old chicks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the facilitation of recall is a consequence of the stress of social isolation.
the facilitatory effect of isolation-stress on memory recall is mediated by glucocorticoid receptors in the chick brain.
the isolation-stress-induced enhancement of passive avoidance memory was a glucocorticoid-dependent effect, which was mediated by a mechanism involving a rapid increase in corticosterone levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the facilitation of passive-avoidance recall by isolation is a stress-induced effect mediated by the glucocorticoid hormone system.
the chick brain has a memory for stress and that the memory can be used to enhance recall of weak learning.
the glucocorticoids facilitate the consolidation of memory for weak passive avoidance learning in chicks, at least in males, but not for stronger versions of the task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stress of isolation, which increases corticosteroid levels, facilitates memory consolidation in chicks, as in mammals.
a brief period of social isolation, a common stressor in the laboratory, is sufficient to facilitate recall of a weak passive avoidance task.
the stress response can enhance memory consolidation, but the mechanism of this enhancement is not clear.
